sections.text:
Lot, peace be upon him, is the nephew of Abraham Al-Khalil, peace be upon him. He believed in his uncle from the beginning and migrated with him from the land of Iraq to the Levant.

God Almighty sent him as a messenger to a people who lived in a group of villages called “Sodom,” located in the present-day Dead Sea region.

Lot's people lived in bliss and prosperity. Their lands were fertile, their crops were abundant, and their trade was thriving.

But instead of thanking God for these successive blessings, they deviated from common sense and committed a heinous crime that no one in the world had ever committed before them.

They brought lust to men rather than women, in a serious setback to human nature and human morality.

They were not satisfied with that, but they were blocking roads, robbing travelers, and bringing evil deeds to their clubs and gatherings without shame or embarrassment.

The Prophet Lot stood among them as a faithful advisor, and began calling on them day and night to return to God and repent from this heinous act.

He said to them: “Do you commit an immoral act that no one of the worlds has ever done before you? Indeed, you commit an indecent act with lust that no one of the worlds has ever done before you. Nay, you are a people. They are extravagant.”

Lot warned them of God's wrath and punishment, and tried to awaken in them the remnants of common sense, but their hearts had become black due to the abundance of sins.

They responded to him with all mockery and insolence and said: “Expel the family of Lot from your village. They are people who purify themselves.”

They went further in their wrongdoing and challenged the Prophet of God, saying: “Bring us the punishment of God if you are truthful.”

Lot had been patient with their harm for many years, and he was pained to see this corruption spreading like wildfire without being able to stop it alone.

Even Lot's wife herself did not believe in him, and she was a traitor to his message, directing her people to his guests so that they could do immoral acts to them.

God responded to Lot’s prayer and supplication, and sent a group of noble angels (including Gabriel and Michael) in the form of extremely beautiful and beautiful young men.

They first went to Abraham and gave him good news about Isaac, and told him that they were going to destroy the villages of Lot’s people because their people were unjust.

The angels arrived in the village of Sodom as guests of Lot, and his people feared for them. As soon as they heard of the presence of Hassan’s youth, they rushed towards Lot’s house, wanting to attack them.

Lot stood in front of his door, defending his guests and trying to stop the people. He said with a sigh: “If only I had strength against you or took shelter in a strong corner.”

Here the angels revealed their true identity and reassured Lot, saying: “O Lot, we are messengers of your Lord, and they will not reach you.”

With the tips of his wing, Gabriel obscured the eyes of the attackers, making them blind and floundering in the dark. They said threateningly: “Tomorrow we will have a business with him!”

The angels ordered Lot to leave the village with his daughters at night, and for none of them to look back, and they told him that the time of their destruction was morning.

Lot left with his family under the cover of darkness, and his unfaithful wife remained with her people to suffer the same fate.

When morning rose, a great disaster befell the people of Sodom.

God commanded Gabriel to raise all seven of their villages with his wings until the angels of heaven heard the crowing of their roosters and the barking of their dogs, then he turned them upside down with tremendous force!
God followed that with stones of baked shale (stones made of clay roasted in the fire of hell), with the names of their companions written on them so that they could be struck with extreme precision.

Lot's people perished, their villages were destroyed and erased from existence, and their place became a lifeless salty lake to remain a sign and lesson for future generations.

The great lesson is that deviating from the nature of God with which He created people brings the most severe types of punishment and destruction.
